items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to find the inverse of the matrix

Content:
[MATH: [1|2; 3|7]]

Content:
We can compute the inverse of [MATH: A] using elementary row operations. There are two key advantages to using row operations to compute the inverse of a matrix:

Content:
1. The method works for any invertible matrix of any size, not just [MATH: 2\times 2] matrices.
2. It requires significantly less computation than some alternative methods. This is especially true for large matrices.

Content:
Here, we'll focus on the [MATH: 2\times 2] case. We use the following fact:

Content:
> The row operations that transform [MATH: A] into the identity matrix [MATH: I_2] also transform [MATH: I_2] into [MATH: A^{-1}].

Content:
So, to find the inverse of [MATH: A,] we proceed as follows:

Content:
Step 1: Write down [MATH: \color{blue}A] and the identity matrix [MATH: I_2] side-by-side, as shown below:
[MATH: 1|2|1|0; 3|7|0|1]

Content:
Step 2: Apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix [MATH: A] into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

Content:
[MATH: [A|I_{2}]|= [1|2|1|0; 3|7|0|1]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} + (− 3)R_{1}; ∼[1|2|1|0; 0|1|− 3|1]|R_{1}|:=R_{1} + (− 2)R_{2}; ∼[1|0|7|− 2; 0|1|− 3|1]; = [I|A^{− 1}]]

Content:
The matrix [MATH: A^{-1}] is obtained on the right-hand side of our big matrix after the transformation. Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: [7|− 2; − 3|1]]

Content:
We can easily check our result by computing [MATH: AA^{-1}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: AA^{− 1}|= [1|2; 3|7][7|− 2; − 3|1] = [1|0; 0|1]✓]

Content:
[MATH: [7|− 2; − 3|1]]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We write down [MATH: A] and the identity matrix [MATH: I] side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix [MATH: A] into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[MATH: [A|I]|= [1|1|1|0; 1|2|0|1]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} + (− 1)R_{1}; ∼[1|1|1|0; 0|1|− 1|1]|R_{1}|:=R_{1} + (− 1)R_{2}; ∼[1|0|2|− 1; 0|1|− 1|1]]

The matrix [MATH: A^{-1}] is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,
[MATH: [2|− 1; − 1|1]]
